name: The SOLID Principles of Object-Oriented Software Design
subject: Object-Oriented Programming Systems

mcqs.question: Which SOLID principle states that high-level modules should depend on abstractions rather than concrete classes?
mcqs.explanation: The Dependency Inversion Principle mandates that high-level policies and low-level details both depend on abstract interfaces.

mcqs.question: Why does a class with 50 different methods for printing, saving to disk, emailing, and user validation violate OOP principles?
options: It violates the Single Responsibility Principle (God Object)
It violates the C++ One Definition Rule
It cannot be stored in an STL vector
It exceeds the operating system process limit
mcqs.explanation: The class has multiple reasons to change (email changes, database changes, printing format changes), directly violating the Single Responsibility Principle.
